purpose: Separate rasterization quality from placement geometry and factual source resolution before expanding the master-render experiment to more product families.

pairwiseDifference.metricScope: absolute RGB difference after reduction to the same 440x180 placement; diagnostic only, not a quality score

interpretation: The current bilinear 4x + box renderer is visibly conservative and is a plausible contributor to weak antialiasing.
Moving from 4x to 8x still produces a material raster change under a higher-order reconstruction path.
Moving from 8x to 12x produces little additional change at placement scale, indicating diminishing returns rather than an unlimited supersampling benefit.
The 450x450 source remains the factual-detail ceiling; a denser or smoother raster cannot recover unsupported hardware texture or geometry.
Edge-gradient diagnostics describe sampling behavior only. They must not be interpreted as factual-resolution or fidelity scores.

decision.nextCandidate: premultiplied cubic reconstruction with an 8x experimental supersampling ceiling
decision.reason: 8x->12x gives marginal placement-scale change relative to cost while source resolution remains unchanged

nextGate: run deterministic self-test for the cubic sampler
human review H45 at master, placement and zoom scales
if H45 passes, run caster 128x128 as the source-resolution negative control before broad rollout
